findings.field: brief.meaningEn / listening, scene, speaking, writing, takeaways
findings.finding: The source itself creatively puts CDs “at the head of the table”, but the lesson treats the phrase as a generally natural rank label for digital passes, small-group practice, food items and menu options. Standard dictionary evidence documents the prominent seat/leader usage; the inanimate product/menu transfer is an inference from this single source, not established as a conventional collocation. “Vegetable meals now sit at the head of the table on the canteen menu” is especially strained and mixes the table-seat image with menu ordering. Retain the exact source, but supply source-specific usage evidence and narrow to natural contexts, or keep this owner on editorial hold; do not exclude automatically under the one-time-comparison rule.

The two models are near paraphrases of the same vegetable/meat menu sentence: both say vegetable mains/meals sit at the head of the table while a few meat dishes remain. Provide genuinely distinct model structures while satisfying the same prompt, if the target passes the naturalness gate.
